text:
alex: incident-bot paged on high tail latency for /v1/generate in us-west-2 — noticed a big spike in 95/99 p95/p99 around 08:04 UTC. customers reporting timeouts.
incident-bot: ALERT: service latency > 1.2s for 5m across topology (incid=INC-2026-03-15-01) :rotating_light:
alex: I'm taking initial triage. attaching quick graphs. looks like continuous batching queue depth jumped and KV cache size exploded.
maria: oncall handover in 10min — if things escalate please page tj. i can stay on until 09:30.
tj: acknowledged, will join if escalated.
alex: quick dump from metrics:
```
# rough numbers from tsdb
time window: 08:00-08:08 UTC
avg_batch_size: 48 -> spike to 140
kv_cache_entries: 24M -> 88M
mem_pressure: 72% -> 96%
node_autoscale_events: 2x scale-up within 3m
```
alex: logs show lots of partial prefixes getting cached; cache eviction isn't keeping up because batcher warmed up aggressively and max_batch_wait decreased after last deploy.
lee: which deploy changed batcher? I think last night emily rolled config to more aggressive batching for cheaper p99 cost.
emily: that was me — I lowered `max_batch_wait_ms` from 30 -> 10 and enabled `continuous_batching:true` for high-throughput models. I measured local perf improvements but didn't stress the KV cache path.
samir: sounds like a regression: continuous batching + aggressive wait reduction leading to richer KV cache variety and memory thrash which spikes GC and slows token generation. Autoscaler sees high CPU/mem and flips nodes too quickly -> thrash.
alex: impact: several customers on dedicated pools saw elevated latency and a few 504s. working on containment: plan A = revert batching config + force TTL prune of KV cache; plan B = temporary HPA dampening to avoid scale thrash.
maria: agree. do we have a safe toggle? emily, can you roll back your change?
emily: 1) I can rollback the config flag on the control plane. 2) I can patch the batcher to cap max_batch_size to 64 as a fast mitigation. Which should I do first?
tj: rollout order: rollback control plane flag first (fastest) -> observe for 2 minutes -> if still high, patch batcher cap -> then run cache eviction.
alex: executing rollback now: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/configs/596/revert -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"fields":["continuous_batching","max_batch_wait_ms"]}'`
ops-bot: deploybot: started config rollback (rollout_id=rb-1765302468-1) by alex.
incident-bot: PAGED alex, maria, tj at 08:06:12 UTC; incident status: acknowledged.
lee: I'm checking autoscaler logs — HPA scaled from 12 -> 20 nodes in <3m, then back down, then up again. Warmup probes failing during scale-up causing additional churn.
samir: actionable: 1) set HPA stabilization window to 5m, 2) set scale_up_cooldown to 180s, 3) add a temporary max_replicas cap for affected pool.
emily: patching control plane now to set `max_batch_wait_ms=30` and `continuous_batching=false` for the model family 'rw-2b'.
ops-bot: deploybot: completed config rollback (rollout_id=rb-1765302468-1) in 18s.
alex: visible improvement: batch sizes dropping back to ~36, queue depth reducing. but KV cache still large — need eviction.
tj: how do we force eviction in prod? we have `kvctl evict` but it's slow. maybe TTL override.
emily: I can trigger GC sweep endpoint: `POST /internal/kv/evict?target=memory_pressure&threshold=0.8` — requires admin token.
alex: do it, emily. also open PR for safer default (max_batch_size and cache watermarks).
emily: sent GC sweep request. ops-bot: gc-sweeper started job job_id=gc-1765302501.
incident-bot: note: operator executed manual eviction (user=emily) at 08:09:58 UTC.
samir: KV entries dropped to 30M within 90s. memory pressure now 68%. p95/p99 latency trending down to normal.
maria: good signal. still seeing autoscale thrash history — we should adjust HPA now to avoid more flips during cooldown. I will apply a temporary HPA change: `stabilizationWindowSeconds=300` and `scaleUpLimit=2` for pool 'dedicated-high'.
lee: doing it now. clusterctl patch hpa/dedicated-high --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/behavior/scaleUp/stabilizationWindowSeconds","value":300}]'
ops-bot: k8s: patch applied to hpa/dedicated-high by lee.
tj: customer impact update: three customers saw >500ms extra latency, one experienced 504s for ~2m. CS notified and incidents created.
alex: handoff: maria, I'm handing incident to you at 08:16 UTC — stay plugged for postmortem. I'm going to regroup with runtime team for root cause analysis.
maria: taking over. will coordinate post-incident follow-up and runbook updates.
emily: follow-ups: add preflight test that simulates continuous-batching + cache churn, add a metric for kv_cache_distinct_prefixes, default max_batch_size=64, and ensure any batching change requires a canary with mem-usage monitors.
samir: also recommend a circuit-breaker: if kv_cache_growth_rate > X then auto-disable continuous batching for that model family.
alex: on the ops side: we'll add a temporary playbook entry: when seeing sudden KV growth + autoscale events, first rollback batching flags, then throttle HPA, then run eviction. Order matters to avoid cascading node churn.
maria: will draft the incident blameless doc and assign owners for each action item. timeline + customer impact + config diffs.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: service metrics returned to baseline at 08:21 UTC (duration ~17m). incident will be auto-closed when postmortem is attached. :white_check_mark:
lee: quick note — we saw one warmup probe failing due to kernel OOM on one node (evicted pods) during the worst window. I'll look into node-level oom-killer tuning.
emily: pushed rollback PR and follow-up config changes: PR#4127.
alex: thanks all. keep pages if anything reoccurs. maria will own next steps.
maria: assigning follow-ups: emily (batcher defaults + canary), lee (node oom tuning), samir (circuit-breaker), alex (playbook updates). closing handoff. :lock:
